prompt_text: Where should I stay in Branson Missouri, an Airbnb or a hotel, and which specific places are best?
answer_verbatim:
Short answer: it depends on what you want from the trip.

Quick decision guide
- Pick a hotel if you want convenience (daily housekeeping), on‑site amenities (pools, restaurants, free breakfast, concierge/ticket help), predictable service, and being close to the Branson Strip or Branson Landing.
- Pick an Airbnb (or private cabin/VRBO) if you want more space, a kitchen, better value for groups/families, more privacy, or a lakefront cabin experience — especially for multi‑night stays or groups.

Which choice is best for common trip types
- Visiting shows/nightlife on the 76 Strip and want to walk to theaters and restaurants: hotel (or a condo right on Branson Landing).
- Family with kids who want theme parks (Silver Dollar City): hotel near Silver Dollar City or a house nearby for space; Keeter Center (see below) is a good family option.
- Want a relaxing lake/cabin experience (boating, fishing, sunsets): Airbnb/VRBO cabin on Table Rock Lake (Hollister, Ridgedale, Indian Point).
- Large groups or a multi‑family trip: Airbnb/large cabin to save money and have shared common spaces.
- A romantic or luxury getaway: upscale resort/hotel with spa and lake views.

Neighborhoods to consider
- 76 Country Boulevard (the Strip): theaters, souvenir shops, easy show access.
- Branson Landing (downtown on Lake Taneycomo): shopping, restaurants, riverfront atmosphere.
- Near Silver Dollar City / College of the Ozarks: best for theme‑park access.
- Table Rock Lake (Hollister, Ridgedale, Indian Point): quiet, lakefront cabins and marinas.
- Big Cedar/Lodge area (south of Branson): high‑end resorts and nature.

Specific recommended places (by type)
Hotels / Resorts — good for convenience, amenities, and reliability
- Big Cedar Lodge (Ridgedale area) — top‑tier resort with cabins, outdoor activities, marina, great if you want a resort experience and don’t mind paying more.
- Chateau on the Lake Resort, Spa & Convention Center — upscale lakeside hotel with spa and lake views.
- Hilton Promenade at Branson Landing — excellent location on the Landing, easy access to shops/restaurants and the lakefront.
- The Keeter Center at College of the Ozarks — family‑friendly, high standards, very convenient for Silver Dollar City and family attractions.

Airbnbs / Cabins — best for privacy, kitchens, groups, and lake time
- Lakefront cabins on Table Rock Lake (search Hollister, Ridgedale, Indian Point) — look for private dock, reviews, and clear check‑in instructions.
- Cabins/large houses near the Strip — good if you want to be close to shows but prefer a full kitchen and common areas.
- Condos at Branson Landing — convenient for nightlife and easy walking to restaurants and the fountain show.

Booking tips and practicalities
- If you’ll be at shows nightly and want simple logistics, pick a hotel on the Strip or at Branson Landing.
- For boating/fishing, you’ll want a property with dock access or nearby marina — verified in the listing.
- For families, indoor pools and free breakfast are a big convenience — search hotels for these amenities.
- On Airbnb: check total price (cleaning + service fee), cancellation policy, parking, and recent reviews (look for many reviews and responses from host).
- Book early for peak season (spring break, summer, fall weekends) — Branson gets busy.
- If you need help finding current listings or a place that fits your budget/party size, tell me: travel dates, number of people, budget per night, and whether you want lakefront/Strip/near Silver Dollar City/pets/accessible rooms. I’ll pull tailored suggestions.
